topics: distance from a point to a line
statement: Find the shortest distance from the point $P(1,1,1)$ to the line through the origin $O$ in the direction $\\mathbf{d}=(1,1,0)$.
solution: The line is $\\mathbf{r}=\\lambda\\mathbf{d}$. The distance is $\\frac{|\\overrightarrow{OP}\\times\\mathbf{d}|}{|\\mathbf{d}|}$. $\\overrightarrow{OP}\\times\\mathbf{d}=(1,1,1)\\times(1,1,0)=(1\\cdot0-1\\cdot1,\\,1\\cdot1-1\\cdot0,\\,1\\cdot1-1\\cdot1)=(-1,1,0)$, magnitude $\\sqrt{2}$. $|\\mathbf{d}|=\\sqrt{2}$. Hence distance $=\\sqrt{2}/\\sqrt{2}=1$.
